prompt:
Two gliders, A and B, move towards each other on a frictionless linear air track.
Glider A of mass 0.400 kg moves to the right at 2.50 m s^-1.
Glider B of mass 0.600 kg moves to the left at 1.50 m s^-1.
After the collision, glider A rebounds to the left with a speed of 1.10 m s^-1.
(a) Calculate the total linear momentum of the two gliders before the collision, taking motion to the right as positive. [1]
(b) Calculate the velocity (magnitude and direction) of glider B after the collision. [2]
hints: Take care with positive and negative signs for velocities.
Equate total initial momentum to total final momentum.
solution:
(a) Taking right as positive: p_total = (0.400 kg x +2.50 m s^-1) + (0.600 kg x -1.50 m s^-1) = +1.000 - 0.900 = +0.100 kg m s^-1 (to the right).
(b) By conservation of momentum:
+0.100 = 0.400 kg x (-1.10 m s^-1) + 0.600 kg x v_B
+0.100 = -0.440 + 0.600 v_B
0.600 v_B = +0.540
v_B = +0.900 m s^-1 (0.900 m s^-1 to the right).
teacher_walkthrough: Step 2: (b) Glider A rebounds to left, so v_A = -1.10 m s^-1.

mark_scheme.criterion: +0.100 kg m s^-1 (or 0.100 kg m s^-1 to the right)
+0.900 m s^-1 (accept 0.90 m s^-1 to the right; must specify direction or positive sign)
